target_customer: Global HIV patients and funders; nonprofit planning to give the vaccine away free, funded by donations and crowdfunding
problem: No effective HIV vaccine existed; the project claimed a machine-learning-designed vaccine targeting T cell responses seen in HIV controllers could be made and distributed cheaply.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by crowdfunding, grants and donations; free vaccine distribution planned

founders.name: Reid Rubsamen
education: Medical doctor, attended Stanford Medical School
founders.background_notes: Per VentureBeat Jan 2014: medical doctor and computer scientist with over 60 drug delivery patents.

founders.name: Naveen Jain
founders.role: Cofounder (listed as CEO on YC page)

founders.name: Ian Cinnamon
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC page; background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Vaccine discovery with a machine-learning epitope selection approach, then animal and human trials, is research-grade and regulatory heavy; outside scientists doubted the concept.

defensibility.rationale: Nonprofit pledging free distribution; the algorithm came from Microsoft Research (Heckerman) and no sourced patents or exclusive data protected the approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; no source shows the project reached trials or was copied.

market_need_then: HIV vaccine was a long-standing unmet need, but VentureBeat in 2014 described the project as a rogue effort and critics questioned its science and promotion.

branding.domain_note: A directory reports that immunityproject.org later lapsed and redirects elsewhere (third party, unverified).

identity.logo: Inspired by The Condom Pledge logo per a wiki mirror
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, crowd and social media oriented

branding.community_and_virality: Crowdfunding videos drew wide press in January 2014; a wiki mirror reports praise from AVAC for fundraising and social media success and criticism from scientists.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong early viral press and a clear mission statement, but criticism from scientists and no sourced lasting brand.

outcome_analysis: Immunity Project drew heavy attention in early 2014 as the second nonprofit in YC, launching a crowdfunding campaign with a 482,000 dollar goal for a final blood experiment before phase one trials. Scientists criticized its team and its promotion over data. No source found shows trial results or a clear end state; the YC directory still lists it as active while a third party says the domain lapsed, so the outcome is not public.
notes: Status Active on YC directory but outcome not public; no company website listed, so no site fetch was possible (dead or none). Funding: crowdfunding raise reported as 402K and YC 20K in a search snippet (unopened), a 120K seed in April 2014 headline from Xconomy (503, not opened), totals of 20K to 1M in aggregators; all unverified and not recorded. Microsoft Research 1M in 2011 is stated by VentureBeat (before the batch). Competitors: no named competitor or incumbent in dated sources; VentureBeat contrasts the neutralizing antibody approach only. Wiki mirror is a secondary source for the logo.
